name: Michael Haneke

name: Vlado Šola

He played for Sesvetski Kraljevac (1984-85) and then RK Medveščak (1985-95), where he learned from teammate Mirko Basic. He was part of Croatia's first-ever national team match against Japan in August 1990 at age 21.

name: Ada Kok
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 100m butterfly European Championship gold at age 15 in 1962, and later won Olympic gold in the 200m butterfly at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics at age 21.
early_history_summary: Inspired by her sister who competed on the Dutch swim team at the 1960 Rome Olympics, Kok became the world's premier butterfly swimmer in the early 1960s. She set nine world records between 1963 and 1967 and was named European Swimmer of the Year in 1963, 1965, and 1967. She won her first European title at age 15 in 1962.
family_context_summary: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands; inspired by her sister who competed on the Dutch swim team at the 1960 Rome Olympics. Family swimming background provided early entry to the sport.

name: Anna Chromý
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Chromý's family was expelled from Czechoslovakia to Austria after WWII and could not afford art school. She only began formal art training after moving to Paris with her husband in 1970 at age 30, studying at the École des Beaux-Arts.
early_history_summary: Born in Český Krumlov, Czechoslovakia (now Czech Republic), Chromý's family was expelled to Austria after WWII when she was five. She grew up in Vienna and Salzburg, where the musical and artistic culture made a lasting impression. Her family could not afford art school, so she worked as a secretary until she married and moved to Paris in 1970, where she finally began studying art at the École des Beaux-Arts and the Académie de la Grande Chaumière.
family_context_summary: Born to a Czech mother and German father in Český Krumlov; family was expelled from Czechoslovakia to Austria after WWII. Family lacked means to send her to art school. She was the last of four girls and inherited artistic talent from her father, who was a musician.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a musician whose artistic sensibility influenced her early creative development, though no direct visual arts training was transferred.
evidence_summary: Chromý was born in Czechoslovakia and expelled to Austria as a child after WWII. Her family could not afford art school, and she worked as a secretary until her husband supported her move to Paris in 1970 at age 30, where she began formal art training. Her mentor Salvador Dalí and her painting career came even later. A 1992 accident forced her to shift from painting to sculpture. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

He worked as a young reporter for Détective Magazine, a runner for L'Express, and from 1970 to 1972 was an editor at Chimie-Actualités, a French chemistry magazine.

name: Miroslav Šatan
milestone_by_age_26: Led the 1994 Winter Olympics in goals with 9 in 8 games for Slovakia at age 19, and later scored 40 goals in the 1998-99 NHL season with the Buffalo Sabres at age 24.
early_history_summary: Šatan played for local club HC Topoľčany as a teenager, scoring 30 goals and 22 assists in 31 games in 1991-92 at age 17. He then joined Dukla Trenčín for the 1992-93 and 1993-94 seasons, where he had a dominant 1993-94 campaign with 42 goals and 64 points in 39 games. He was drafted 111th overall by the Edmonton Oilers in the 1993 NHL Entry Draft and represented Slovakia at the 1994 Winter Olympics, leading the tournament in goals.
family_context_summary: Born in Jacovce, Czechoslovakia (now Slovakia). Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Slovak hockey pipeline, Dukla Trenčín, early specialization, goal-scoring prodigy, Slovakia independence
evidence_summary: Šatan emerged from the Slovak hockey system, playing for HC Topoľčany and then Dukla Trenčín as a teenager. At age 19, he led the 1994 Winter Olympics in goals with 9 in 8 games for newly independent Slovakia, a remarkable international achievement. He was drafted by the Edmonton Oilers in 1993 and debuted in the NHL in 1995-96, later scoring 40 goals for Buffalo in 1998-99. The breakup of Czechoslovakia meant Slovakia had to climb from the C Pool of the World Championships, adding adversity to his early career. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
